pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Sketch the worker pool: which goroutines exist, which channels connect them, and who closes each channel? What goes wrong if a worker closes the results channel?
expected_points: feeder sends jobs and closes the jobs channel (only sender closes)
N workers range over jobs, send results, exit when jobs closes
a closer goroutine does wg.Wait then closes results, because only the WaitGroup knows when all senders are done
a worker closing results panics another worker's send

questions.prompt: What is a goroutine leak, and name two ways a worker pool can leak. What discipline prevents them?
expected_points: a goroutine blocked forever on a channel nobody will service again, holding memory invisibly
examples: jobs channel never closed (workers stuck in range), results never closed (collector stuck), send with no receiver
for every channel know who closes it and why every send finds a receive

questions.prompt: State errgroup's contract: what happens when one function fails, what does Wait return, and when does Wait return? Which primitives did your mini version need?
expected_points: first non-nil error is kept, later errors dropped
first error cancels the derived context so siblings can stop early
Wait blocks until every function returns — cancellation is a request, not a kill — then returns the first error
built from WaitGroup, sync.Once for the first error, and context.CancelFunc

questions.prompt: A buffered channel can be a semaphore — how? And given both cap concurrency at N, when do you reach for a semaphore instead of a worker pool?
expected_points: buffered channel of capacity n: Acquire sends (blocks when full), Release receives; the buffer is the count
pool owns long-lived workers pulling a queue — for a stream of homogeneous jobs
semaphore caps goroutines that already exist (e.g. one per request) without restructuring
TryAcquire via select/default enables load-shedding a pool queue can't express

questions.prompt: Walk through graceful shutdown's three steps in your Queue, and explain why Submit needs a mutex-guarded flag rather than just checking a boolean.
expected_points: stop accepting, drain in-flight work, bounded wait via select on done vs ctx.Done
send on a closed channel panics, so the closed flag and the close must be coordinated under one mutex
wg.Wait wrapped in a goroutine closing a done channel makes waiting selectable
on deadline it returns ctx.Err and stops waiting — the stuck goroutine is not killed

questions.prompt: Pick a pattern and justify it via backpressure and failure handling: (a) a service resizing an endless stream of uploaded images; (b) rendering one page that needs five API calls, useless unless all succeed.
expected_points: (a) worker pool: bounded workers, the jobs channel queues and blocks producers when saturated, one failed image is just a result
(b) errgroup: first failure cancels the other four fetches, one Wait returns the error
justification names who blocks under load and what one failure does to the rest

questions.prompt: Why does errgroup's Wait cancel the derived context even when every function succeeded?
expected_points: a derived context holds resources until cancelled — never cancelling leaks them
same hygiene vet's lostcancel check enforces on ordinary WithCancel code
after Wait nothing should still be using the group context, so cancelling is free
